Subject: Post-demo: hosted evaluation scope and sandbox access

Hi Ami / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

Recap from our call:
- PayFlow is evaluating a hosted-first approach for the first phase (customer-facing chat & invoice summarization).
- Primary constraints: sub-200ms token latency targets for short interactions, bursty QPS around 80–120 reqs/s during peak batch jobs, and strict data retention requirements in your region.
- Future stages may look at Dedicated capacity if sustained throughput or on-prem if regulatory constraints tighten.

What we can provide immediately (next 48 hours):
- A hosted sandbox endpoint with scoped API keys for functional testing and load-profile sampling.
- Our hosted quickstart playbook (attached) that outlines endpoint mapping, example batching, and prefix/KV-cache guidance.
- A preliminary ratecard and recommended thresholds for the trial (attached).

Asks from your side:
- Confirm the evaluation window you’d like to run (we recommend 2–3 weeks for meaningful throughput sampling).
- Approximate QPS pattern during your peak batch run (avg/peak tokens per second or requests per second).
- Any procurement or security contacts we should loop in now (I’ve copied procurement if that’s the right address).

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) I’ll provision sandbox API keys and send credentials (Aditya will attach technical notes on limits).
2) You schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive with your infra/eng + our infra lead (suggested window: Mon/Tue next week).
3) Run a 48-hour functional + 48-hour load sample and share logs so we can tune batching/kv-cache.

Attachments included: redwood_hosted_quickstart_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook), hosted_ratecards_v1.pdf (trial rate guidance).

If that all looks good, reply with the evaluation window and a quick note on peak QPS and we’ll get keys out.

Thanks,
Monica

Monica —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we kick off the sandbox: 

1) Sandbox vs production rate limits: what are the default throttles you apply to sandbox API keys vs production hosted keys? We want to set internal expectations for load tests.
2) Token economics: rough hosted cost estimate for 1M tokens at the trial rate (ballpark is fine).
3) KV/prefix caching behavior: does the hosted sandbox support prefix/KV cache modes identical to production? Will caching behavior be representative for our eval?
4) Can you confirm whether sandbox endpoints are reachable from our AWS us-west-2 VPC without special IP allowlisting? If there’s a connectivity requirement we’ll loop in networking.

Evaluation window: we want to start the week of May 25 (target 2 weeks). Peak numbers: our customer-facing chat (short-turn) is expected to see ~100–150 rps during scheduled spikes; average during working hours ~20–30 rps. For the batch job (daily ingestion), we’ll be doing bursts up to ~10k tokens/sec for short periods.

Procurement: I’ve cc’d procurement@payflow.com — they’ll follow up on terms if we proceed beyond sandbox.

Thanks — happy to take the tech deep-dive early next week.

—Ami

Hi Ami — quick technical answers and what we’ll include in the sandbox package: 

1) Sandbox vs production throttles:
- Sandbox (trial keys): default soft-limits for functional tests: 60 reqs/s and 250k tokens/min per key. These are adjustable on request for the evaluation window once we confirm load profile.
- Hosted production: configurable quotas by plan; baseline hosted entry tier supports 500 reqs/s and 2M tokens/min per tenant with autoscaling and burst capacity available.

2) Token economics (trial estimate):
- For the sandbox/trial we provide a credit-based token allowance. For a rough number: at our standard hosted pricing, 1M inference tokens ≈ $120 (model-dependent); we will send an exact per-model estimate in the ratecard attachment. Trial credits won’t bill you for test usage.

3) KV/prefix caching parity:
- Sandbox supports identical prefix and KV-cache semantics as production (same eviction/TTL defaults). Cache hit rates in sandbox are representative; for best fidelity run the 48h sample with the same prompt prefixes you expect in prod.

4) Network reachability:
- Sandbox endpoints are publicly reachable over HTTPS. For lower-latency routing we recommend calling from us-west-2. No special IP allowlisting needed for basic tests; if your security policy requires fixed egress IPs we can provide a managed egress IP list or set up a private peering flow in Dedicated/Private evaluations.

Additional notes: 
- Canary/fallback behavior: during your sample we can enable canary routing to a smaller model variant if we detect warm-up latency issues — that’s a config toggle we can flip during the test.
- Autoscaling: hosted autoscaling is driven by request concurrency and queue depth; our ops team will watch the 48h load window and suggest batching/kv-cache adjustments to hit the 200ms short-turn target.

Attachments included in this reply: sandbox-credentials.txt (scoped keys & endpoints), hosted_ratecards_v1.pdf (detailed model rates). I’ll provision the sandbox keys by tomorrow morning and share the key+endpoint in a follow-up email.

Proposed tech deep-dive: May 27, 10:00–11:00 PT. If that works, Monica can send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
